_comment: Ruleset 3 of 5 — Tag protection for releases.
Applies to refs/tags/v* — the tags .github/release-drafter.yml creates when
a maintainer publishes a draft release.
WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS
A tag is what an artifact claims to be. If a tag can be moved or re-pushed
after the fact, then 'v1.0.0' stops meaning 'the commit we reviewed and
shipped' and any downstream consumer — a Docker image, a Vercel build, a
student's fork pinned to a release — is trusting a mutable pointer.
deletion      — a deleted release tag removes the only durable pointer to
non_fast_forward — a force-pushed tag silently rewrites history.
update        — re-pointing an existing tag at a different commit.
so 'v1', 'v1.2' and 'latest' cannot be published by
accident. Semver is what CHANGELOG.md promises.
Note: the pattern applies to tags matched by the conditions below (v*), so
a tag such as 'v1' is now rejected at push time rather than being created
and forgotten. Cut prereleases as v1.2.0-rc.1.
name: Protect release tags
